TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate.rationale: The phase loss this entry recorded is gone. C# runs Hook.ModifyEnergyCostInCombat as two complete listener passes -- every TryModifyEnergyCostInCombat (Hook.cs:1580-1583) and then every TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate (Hook.cs:1584-1587) -- and Corruption is in the second (CorruptionPower.cs:16). The sim now reproduces exactly that: HookSystem._each (sts2_rl/hooks.py:153-180) re-walks the ordered listener list once per suffix in _PHASES order (hooks.py:36), HookSystem.modify_card_energy_cost (hooks.py:391-395) is a _each consumer, and CorruptionPower declares `modify_card_energy_cost_late` (powers.py:648) rather than the plain method, so its hard 0 lands strictly after every plain-pass modifier (relics/spiked_gauntlets.py:26-31, and the ported Curious/Tangled powers) regardless of registration or acquisition order -- confirmed by execution (`_phase_hooks(CorruptionPower)` == {'modify_card_energy_cost'}, cost 0 in both application orders) and by test/test_hook_order.py's passing energy-cost order tests.  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: PHASE LOSS. This is a phase-suffixed C# hook and the sim has a single unphased dispatch, which is hook_dispatch gap G3 (24 dispatchers lose their phase structure; 27 phase-suffixed hooks declared on AbstractModel). Per binding rule 3 the mechanism keeps G3's `gap` verdict and is cross-referenced rather than re-argued. Third-file citations, not hashed here. Corruption is a LATE-phase cost modifier: C# runs it in Hook.ModifyEnergyCostInCombat's second pass (TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate, CorruptionPower.cs:16-25), strictly after every early-phase modifier. The sim's single modify_card_energy_cost pass orders it by registration instead, so Corruption contends with the ported early-phase modifiers -- Curious (powers.py:2883) and Spiked Gauntlets -- by accident of application order. Corruption returning a hard 0 makes it order-sensitive in the worst way: it must WIN over Spiked Gauntlets' +1, and it does so only if it happens to be registered later. Same shape as hook_dispatch G3's own executed Tangled/Free-Attack witness.

ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition.issue: Closed 2026-08-01 (tier-2 round 13, R5 fix pass). All three named residues are gone: CorruptionPower is now a modify_card_play_result_pile listener returning 'exhaust' -- CorruptionPower.cs:27-38 VERBATIM (owner test, card.Type != Skill test, return (PileType.Exhaust, position); NO pile-membership test and no pileType != Discard guard of any kind). (1) Rebound's stack is no longer unconditionally consumed: the chain is seeded with GetResultPileTypeForCardPlay (CardModel.cs:2070-2082 via :1890's defaultPileType), so with Corruption applied first Rebound is handed 'exhaust', abstains at ReboundPower.cs:25-28 and is never credited -- executed BOTH orders, rebound.amount 2 vs 1, which is Hook.cs:1401-1404 reproduced: C#'s ORDER-INDEPENDENT pile with C#'s ORDER-DEPENDENT stack. (2) The exhaust move happens ONCE at the play's exit switch (CardModel.cs:1985), not once per play-count iteration from on_card_played, so a replayed Skill stays in PileType.Play for every iteration and fires exactly one Hook.AfterCardExhausted. (3) Corruption is on the chain, so the modifiers notification set matches. WHAT REASONING THIS REPLACES: the round-13 review had already replaced the original order-dependence framing (correctly -- C# is order-independent on the pile and Corruption wins there too); what closes here is the remaining 'the REAL open work is architectural and BLOCKED-ON-FOOTPRINT'. It landed, in the exact shape that hand-off specified.  The text it replaced read: STAYS OPEN, LIVE -- but the recorded reasoning is REPLACED (2026-08-01, round 13, R3 + its review). The record framed the divergence as order-dependence: that the sim lets Corruption always beat Nostalgia. THAT FRAMING IS WRONG and would have sent the hooks.py/combat.py owner to build the wrong thing: CorruptionPower.cs:27-38 carries no pileType guard while NostalgiaPower.cs:39-42 and ReboundPower.cs:25-28 both bail on a non-Discard incoming pile, so C# is order-independent too and Corruption wins there as well. The sim's final pile is already faithful. The REAL open work is architectural and BLOCKED-ON-FOOTPRINT: hooks.py needs an 'exhaust' pile-destination value on the modify_card_play_result_pile chain and combat.py needs the post-loop dispatch for it, so Corruption stops hand-moving the card inside the play loop. power/rebound's 2026-08-01 fix is the template. Do NOT build 'let application order decide the winner' -- it already doesn't, in either engine.  The text it replaced read: The destination-pile DECISION is replaced by an after-the-fact move, and the sim has the right hook available and does not use it. C# (CorruptionPower.cs:27-38) returns (PileType.Exhaust, position) from the pile-resolution chain, so a played Skill never enters the discard pile at all. The sim lets combat._resolve_card_play put the card in the discard pile (combat.py:453), runs the exhaust-keyword check and then the modify_card_play_result_pile chain (combat.py:500-511), and only afterwards -- inside on_card_played (combat.py:514) -- does Corruption pull the card out of the discard pile and append it to the exhaust pile, firing on_card_exhausted itself (powers.py:610-613). Two consequences. (i) CONTENTION ORDER: the sim's modify_card_play_result_pile hook exists (hooks.py:236-246) but accepts only 'discard'/'draw_top', so Nostalgia (powers.py:3595-3612) runs FIRST and can move the Skill to the top of the draw pile, after which Corruption's `card in player.discard_pile` test fails (powers.py:610) and the Skill is never exhausted. In C# both are listeners on ONE chain and the last writer wins, so Corruption exhausts it. Both Nostalgia and Corruption are ported Ironclad-pool powers, so the contention is reachable; which one wins in C# is hook_dispatch G2's listener-order question and is not re-verdicted here. (ii) EVENT TIMING: Feel No Pain and Dark Embrace see on_card_exhausted fired from the middle of Corruption's on_card_played rather than at pile assignment, so their effects land after any on_card_played listener registered before Corruption. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
